clips.send: Dont mix up: “An eye for an eye” applied only between people of the same class. The Code divided people into ranks, and the same injury was punished very differently for a noble, a commoner or an enslaved person — it protected the ruling class. It is the oldest fairly complete written law code to survive, but not the oldest law code: the earlier Code of Ur-Nammu survives only in pieces.

clips.send: Archaeologists have dug up the workers’ town at Giza: bakeries, breweries and the workers’ own tombs. So the builders were mainly organised, fed and paid workers plus farmers serving in shifts — not whipped slaves as in old movies. During the Nile flood, when the fields were under water, lots of farmers were free to work.

clips.send: Dont mix up: “Mesopotamia” (Greek for “between the rivers”) is a region — the land between the Euphrates and the Tigris, mostly in today’s Iraq — not a country. Babylon was one kingdom (and city) inside it. Egypt is in north-east Africa; Mesopotamia is in south-west Asia. Pyramids were tombs for pharaohs; Mesopotamia’s stepped towers, ziggurats, were temples.

clips.send: 易错点：“以眼还眼”只适用于身份相同的人之间。法典把人分成不同等级，同样的伤害，对贵族、平民和奴隶的处罚完全不同——它维护的是奴隶主阶级的利益。《汉谟拉比法典》是现存世界上第一部比较完整的成文法典，但不是最早的法典：更早的《乌尔纳姆法典》只留下了残片。
